statement: Pushing back on a student's plan to keep only 1000 keys in memory, the teacher said there is no reason to limit memory to 1000 keys: far more keys can be kept in memory.
detail: This comes just before the teacher calls the B+ tree / 8 KB block proposal over-engineering. It anticipates the later estimate that the whole index (about 1.75 MB) fits in RAM.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: why only 1000 keys in memory? So I can keep a lot.
flags: check: speaker of "So I can keep a lot" (may be Student 2 replying; the teacher continues "No, why I'm saying this is")

statement: The chosen update transition is a parallel setup: the new dictionary is prepared and uploaded as a separate file at a new path while the old file keeps being served, and the API servers then move over to it.
detail: A student had argued (01:19:40-01:21:12) that a rolling upgrade on the single file in one place would not work and proposed a complete A-to-B switch: build the new file at a new S3 URL, hand the new address to the API servers, then roll it out (e.g. canary). The teacher names the approach in his notes recap: "parallel setup. This is what we are doing as parallel setup."
case_study: Word dictionary on S3: applying the weekly Oxford changelog to the one-file dictionary served by the API servers.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: parallel setup. This is what we are doing as parallel setup.

statement: Letting the class brainstorm options that end up rejected is useful: it shows why certain design decisions are made.
detail: Said while cutting the meta.json/updated_at discussion short to converge faster ("Otherwise, we would spend till 11.30 on this").
speaker: teacher
verbatim: But it's good that you folks are thinking. Why are we making certain decisions? Now we understand.

statement: When integrity is ignored, systems only seem to work fine; in reality they do not, and without the occasional engineer who thinks about integrity everything goes for a toss.
detail: Said right after the point that system design overviews never cover integrity and that only one passionate engineer usually thinks about it; database internals do deal with it.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: Otherwise it's all gone for a toss. Work just fine. But in reality, it does not.
flags: check: garbled phrasing "Work just fine. But in reality, it does not."
